title: Security posture discovery - Meridian Capital
next_steps: Send SOC 2 + ISO 27001 certs and evidence pack
Share VPC/private deployment diagram and network requirements
Schedule technical deep-dive for benchmarks and latency tests week of 2026-03-29
action_items: Ethan Morales: send pricing, SOC2 & ISO docs by 2026-03-22
Priya Nair: prepare sample benchmark plan + test matrix by 2026-03-25
Mark Benson: share current VPC architecture and list of blocked IPs by 2026-03-24
summary: Intro discovery focusing on security requirements for evaluating Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Meridian's primary concerns: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML integration, RBAC and fine-grained access controls, audit logs and retention, encryption with KMS/HSM, and data residency/retention policy. Redwood AE/SE outlined hosted baseline, dedicated reserved capacity, and private VPC/on-prem options and proposed follow-ups: send compliance artifacts, network diagram, and schedule deep-dive benchmarks.
transcript:
[00:00] Ethan Morales: Hey everyone, thanks for joining - I'm Ethan from Redwood, AE on the account. With me is Priya, our solutions engineer. How's everyone doing?
[00:08] Laura Kim: Hi Ethan, thanks. Quick heads up - Rajiv is on from security, Mark's on infra. We wanted to do a security posture deep dive before moving to pricing.
[00:15] Ethan Morales: Perfect, that's exactly what we wanted to cover. Our goal is to walk through SOC2/ISO, SSO options, RBAC, audit logs, encryption/KMS, and data retention. Priya will chime in for the tech details.
[00:28] Priya Nair: Hey, hi - quick FYI I'll probably ask some clarifying infra questions as we go.
[00:33] Rajiv Gupta: Cool. To start, do you have SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001? We get asked for evidence during vendor reviews.
[00:40] Ethan Morales: Yes, Redwood holds SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001; we can share the cert and the bridge letter. I'll attach the evidence pack after this call.
[00:48] Laura Kim: Great. Also curious - for hosted versus dedicated, what's the difference in terms of log access and auditability?
[00:55] Priya Nair: On hosted, we surface audit logs via the console and you get standardized retention - but you don't get raw host-level logs. For Dedicated and Private, we can provide access to richer audit streams and custom retention via log forwarding or a S3 export. We also support syslog/CloudWatch export.
[01:10] Mark Benson: When you say 'audit logs', do you include token-level request traces and who triggered them? We need user-level for compliance.
[01:18] Priya Nair: Yes, we capture token-level request metrics, request IDs, route/model used, and the authenticated principal - when integrated with SSO/SCIM SAML. For Dedicated/Private you can push raw audit events to your SIEM. On Hosted we also provide the events but access patterns are via the console or secure exports.
[01:35] Rajiv Gupta: SSO is important - we use Okta and require SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning. How's your SAML support?
[01:42] Ethan Morales: We support SAML 2.0 SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Setup is straightforward: metadata exchange, certs, and you can map groups to RBAC roles. We'll send the SAML integration guide.
[01:52] Laura Kim: Mapping groups to roles - does Redwood support granular RBAC? We need to ensure devs can't access production keys or private model configs.
[02:00] Priya Nair: Yes, our RBAC supports role templates and custom roles. You can separate 'admin', 'read-only', 'model-deployer', and 'billing' roles, and you can restrict access to specific projects or environments. For Dedicated and Private, we also support IP allowlists at the tenant level.
[02:17] Mark Benson: And what about KMS & HSM? We must keep customer keys in our KMS and not have plaintext anywhere in Redwood.
[02:25] Priya Nair: For Private we can integrate with your KMS/HSM (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault, or customer-managed HSM). For Dedicated we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) integration so keys are in your KMS. For Hosted, by default we manage envelope encryption keys, but we do support a BYOK option for customers on enterprise plans.
[02:46] Rajiv Gupta: So with BYOK, do you ever see unencrypted model cache or token data on disk?
[02:52] Priya Nair: We encrypt all at rest; KV cache and model artifacts are stored encrypted. With BYOK, the root key stays in your KMS and Redwood only has wrapped keys - we don't have access to plaintext root keys. There are nuances for in-memory caches - we avoid persisting plaintext to disk, but as with any runtime, secrets may be in memory during inference. We can discuss hardened memory and HSM protected inference in Private deployments.
[03:18] Laura Kim: Data residency - we operate in EU and US; we need guarantees that certain datasets never leave EU. What options do we have?
[03:26] Ethan Morales: We support region pinning. Hosted clusters in EU-only regions keep data within the region; for strict residency we recommend Dedicated in-region pools or Private (VPC/on-prem) where everything is in your controlled network. We'll include region SOC documentation and our regioning policies.
[03:41] Mark Benson: On retention - we have a 90-day retention rule for PII-derived logs and a separate 7-year archive for audit logs. Can Redwood customize retention policies?
[03:50] Priya Nair: Yes - we can set retention per log type. Hosted has standard tiers but enterprise accounts can request custom retention. For Dedicated/Private you have full control and can forward to your long-term archive (S3/Glacier). We'll need to map events types to retention classes in the next steps.
[04:07] Rajiv Gupta: Encryption in transit - do you enforce mTLS between clients and the API?
[04:12] Priya Nair: We provide TLS 1.2/1.3 by default. For Dedicated/Private we can enable mTLS and private endpoints inside your VPC.
[04:21] Laura Kim: What's your logging fidelity? We need immutability and tamper-evidence for audit logs.
[04:28] Priya Nair: We support WORM-style export to S3 with object lock for immutability. We also provide signed log digests for integrity verification for enterprise accounts.
[04:39] Ethan Morales: Quick question back to you - what are the main blockers for selecting Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private for Meridian? Is it mostly compliance or also performance/cost?
[04:48] Laura Kim: A mix. Compliance is the primary driver - Rajiv's team needs evidence. But we're also worried about latency for low-latency trading features and cost predictability.
[04:57] Mark Benson: Right, our infra team likes reserved capacity because we can guarantee throughput during market open.
[05:03] Priya Nair: That lines up: Hosted is fastest to onboard and lower up-front cost, Dedicated gives reserved GPU pools and more control over logs/retention, Private gives the highest control for KMS/HSM + network isolation. For latency-sensitive cases we can pin models to dedicated pools in-region to meet your SLOs.
[05:20] Rajiv Gupta: Regarding compliance evidence - is there an audit portal or do we get a package?
[05:25] Ethan Morales: We provide both: a compliance evidence package (certs, audit reports, policy documents) and an auditor liaison for enterprise customers. There's also an SOC2 report you can share under an NDA.
[05:37] Laura Kim: Network setup - we use strict egress controls. We'll need a list of IPs and CIDR ranges for allowed outbound, and ideally private peering.
[05:45] Priya Nair: We can provide static IP ranges for Dedicated and Private peering. Hosted uses a dynamic fleet in the region, but we offer NAT gateway options and we can set up private peering for enterprise. We'll follow up with a network diagram and the CIDR/IP ranges.
[05:59] Mark Benson: For Private on-prem deployment, what is the ops footprint? We have air-gapped requirements for some teams.
[06:06] Priya Nair: For on-prem we provide a package and a deployment runbook. Air-gapped installs are supported; they require additional setup for model updates, but we have a documented process. Ops can be managed by your team; Redwood offers an optional managed private plane for customers who want us to run it inside their network under tight SLA.
[06:26] Laura Kim: Any third-party pen testing or vulnerability scans we should know about?
[06:31] Ethan Morales: We do quarterly vulnerability scanning and annual pen tests; results can be shared under NDA. We can also coordinate a customer-specific scoping for red-team exercises.
[06:41] Rajiv Gupta: What's your incident response SLA and how do we get notified?
[06:45] Priya Nair: We have defined incident response playbooks; Sev1 incidents get pager-level escalation and a postmortem. We can integrate with your incident channels (PagerDuty, Slack). We also produce forensic artifacts and will provide timelines per SLA.
[06:58] Ethan Morales: Switching to auth details - do you need service accounts or just user SSO?
[07:03] Mark Benson: We mainly use service accounts for downstream systems; devs use SSO. We need to ensure service accounts have limited privileges and keys rotate.
[07:11] Priya Nair: We support short-lived tokens, scoped API keys, and service accounts with restricted scopes. API keys can be rotated automatically and audited. For high security, you can require KMS-wrapped tokens and rotate keys via your KMS.
[07:28] Laura Kim: About data access for model outputs - we generate sensitive derived data. Can Redwood guarantee that hosted models won't use our data for training or logging?
[07:38] Ethan Morales: Redwood does not use customer data for model training. By default, hosted telemetry is used for product telemetry and performance, but customers can opt out of telemetry collection. For Dedicated/Private, isolation is stronger - telemetry stays in your environment. We'll send our data usage and retention policy.
[07:58] Rajiv Gupta: Can we have explicit contract language about data not being used for model training, and required breach notifications within a certain window?
[08:05] Ethan Morales: Yes, those contract clauses are standard requests; our legal/enterprise team handles SLA & breach notification timelines. I'll flag that for the contract review.
[08:15] Mark Benson: Can you detail how audit logs are correlated with authentication logs? For us we want end-to-end traceability from a user action to the model call.
[08:25] Priya Nair: We emit correlated request IDs and include user principal in the event. When integrated with SSO/SCIM mapping, you get user IDs. For service accounts we embed the service principal. All events include timestamps, request latency, model version and route. For Dedicated you can get the raw event stream for SIEM ingestion.
[08:46] Laura Kim: Any limitations on redaction or PII scrubbing? We may want logs scrubbed at ingest.
[08:52] Priya Nair: We have server-side redaction rules and client-side pre-filtering. You can configure masking rules and we can implement pre-ingest scrubbers in Private deployments. We'll need to discuss which fields to redact.
[09:05] Rajiv Gupta: What's the model lifecycle - if you update a model, how are regressions detected and can we pin versions?
[09:12] Ethan Morales: Customers can pin to a model version; Redwood has rollout controls (canary, A/B) and automatic fallbacks. We also provide quality monitoring tied to prompt sets so regressions trigger alerts. We'll share docs on versioning and rollouts.
[09:27] Mark Benson: For the benchmark Priya mentioned, we'll want to test 99th percentile latency, throughput under burst, and cold-starts. Can you run a PoC with us?
[09:36] Priya Nair: Absolutely. We'll propose a test matrix: p99 latency, median, token cost, and throughput with realistic prompt shapes. For Dedicated we can allocate a pilot pool. Priya: I'll draft the matrix and share.
[09:50] Ethan Morales: Ok to recap next steps - I'll send SOC2/ISO artifacts, SAML integration guide, and the network diagram. Priya will share a benchmark plan. Mark, you'll send VPC details.
[09:58] Mark Benson: Yes. Also, can you include pricing for hosted, a committed Dedicated plan, and a rough estimate for private deployment? We need to budget.
[10:06] Ethan Morales: We'll include a pricing sheet. For Dedicated we'll provide reserved capacity tiers and burst options. For Private we'll give a ballpark plus professional services estimates.
[10:16] Rajiv Gupta: One more question - do you support attestation for supply chain (SBOM) and software bill of materials for the runtime images? We have to produce SBOMs.
[10:25] Priya Nair: Yes, we produce SBOMs for enterprise customers and can provide runtime image fingerprints and patch timelines.
[10:33] Laura Kim: Great. Any immediate blockers from Redwood side to run the PoC?
[10:38] Priya Nair: No blockers - just access to a small sample dataset, network allowlist, and the set of prompts you want to evaluate. We'll avoid sharing sensitive data and can operate on masked datasets.
[10:49] Ethan Morales: Perfect. We'll follow up with the attachments and set the deep-dive calendar invite. Thanks everyone for your time.
[10:55] Rajiv Gupta: Thanks all. Looking forward to the docs.
[11:00] Laura Kim: Thanks - talk soon.
[11:04] (meeting ends)

Notes: Transcript contains typical auto-transcription artifacts (occasional word swaps), references to KV cache appear as "KV cash" or similar in earlier internal notes; timestamps approximate. Customers requested: SOC2+ISO evidence, SAML/SCIM guide, network CIDR list, benchmark plan, pricing for hosted/dedicated/private, and contract language for data non-use and breach notification.
